root_cause.text: In `hci_le_create_big_complete_evt()`, the loop index `i` is not validated against `ev->num_bis` before accessing `ev->bis_handle[i]`, causing an out-of-bounds read when the controller provides fewer bis_handles than expected, leading to an infinite loop as connections remain in `BT_BOUND` state.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "there is no check that i stays within ev->num_bis before the array access." The patch adds the check `if (ev->num_bis <= i)` to prevent the OOB read and subsequent infinite loop.

candidates.rationale: Direct out-of-bounds read: accesses ev->bis_handle[i] without verifying i < ev->num_bis, allowing read past the array.
The if condition leads to the vulnerable access but does not check that i is within the bounds of ev->bis_handle, enabling the out-of-bounds read.
If the out-of-bounds read results in a failed hci_conn_set_handle, the continue skips updating conn->state, leaving connections in BT_BOUND and causing an infinite loop.
Uses i to decide termination; if i has been incremented beyond ev->num_bis due to the out-of-bounds access, this check may incorrectly prevent cleanup, contributing to the infinite loop.

Setting the state to BT_CONNECTED relies on a successful handle assignment; if the out-of-bounds read causes a false success, some connections may never reach this state and remain BT_BOUND, perpetuating the loop.
